bib.title: Chain of Code: Reasoning with a Language Model-Augmented Code Emulator

SOURCE: "Chain of Code: Reasoning with a Language Model-Augmented Code Emulator", Chengshu Li, Jacky Liang, Andy Zeng, Xinyun Chen, Karol Hausman, Dorsa Sadigh, Sergey Levine, Li Fei-Fei, Fei Xia, Brian Ichter. Venue: Proceedings of the 41st ICML, Vienna, PMLR 235, 2024 (arXiv:2312.04474v4, 29 Jul 2024; first posted Dec 2023).

COVERAGE: All 19 pages, 74,336 chars read. Body, limitations, appendices A.1-A.6 and the tables were all read. References were skimmed (page 9 to 11). Figure data (bar plots, Figs 2, 4-7) is not in the text extraction, so only the tables give numbers. I also read the target note: 03-core-techniques.md. Its PAL section and its Sprague GSM8K-Hard numbers are the natural home for this paper. It does not cite Chain of Code or arXiv 2312.04474 yet.

CLAIMS (ranked)

  setup: 23 BBH tasks, few-shot with 3 examples from the same task, text-davinci-003. PaLM 2-S (code variant) gets 78 (CoC), 61 (CoT) and 49 (direct).
  quote: "Single task 68 55 72 (+17) 84 (+29) 49 61 (+12) 78 (+29)"
  where: Table 1, p6 (also Table A1, p12)
- claim: On algorithmic tasks CoC scores 95% against 71% for CoT. On NLP tasks it ties CoT (74 vs 74), and it is no better there.
  number: 95 vs 71 algorithmic; 74 vs 74 NLP
  setup: BBH task categories from Suzgun et al., text-davinci-003, interweave variant
  quote: "Algorithmic Task (avg)λ 21 64 92 41 71 95 95 92 80 58 50" and "NLP Task (avg)κ 30 71 97 67 74 74 70 68 18 68 63"

  number: 84 vs 48 (Python only), 57 (LM only), 63 (LM state), 82 and 80 (try-Python-except-LM variants)

LIMITS
- The authors concede that it "requires additional context length and computation time" (two-step generate-then-execute with interweaving). It can also hurt: "there are few tasks in which code doesn't help, e.g., the task Ruin Names".
- The LM cannot modify custom Python objects during simulation, because state is tracked as strings parsed to built-in types (dict, tuple).
- Safety: the impact statement says it runs LLM output "as if they are always benign code", and needs safeguards before deployment. This bears on the note's `exec` pitfall.
- The headline results use text-davinci-003 and PaLM 2-S (code variant), both dated completion models. Few-shot BBH with 3 examples is the main paradigm. The authors say instruction-tuned models were "non-trivial" to elicit CoC from. The gpt-4 gap narrows to +3 over CoT when few-shot (91 vs 88).
- Cross-task on PaLM 2-S shows no gain (47 vs 47). No variance or seeds are reported, and the BBH figures are single numbers.
- Only a single "human" baseline is used (Srivastava et al., 2022 average raters, who had no code access). The claim of beating humans is therefore against raters without tools.
- "SoTA 84%" is relative to the Gemini report, as of Dec 2023, and has dated.
- Robotics results are qualitative only.
- The instruction-tuned comparisons in A.3 and A.4 are not matched in prompt shots (see the quote above).
- Not tested: whether an LM emulation of a line is faithful. The LMulator output is a model guess, not computation, so semantic lines inherit the usual LM errors. The paper does not measure emulation accuracy separately.

BUILDS ON (as printed)
- Chain of Thought (Wei et al., 2022b); least-to-most (Zhou et al., 2022a); "let's think step by step" (Kojima et al., 2022); "Take a deep breath..." (Yang et al., 2023).
- ScratchPad (Nye et al., 2021), credited as the first demonstration of the code-simulation ability the LMulator needs.
- Program of Thoughts (Chen et al., 2022) and Program-aided Language Models (Gao et al., 2023), the Python-only baseline.
- BIG-Bench (Srivastava et al., 2022) and BIG-Bench Hard (Suzgun et al., 2022); GSM8K (Cobbe et al., 2021).
- Code as Policies (Liang et al., 2023) for the robotics side. In-context learning (Brown et al., 2020). Min et al., 2022 is cited for format-change robustness.
- Tree/Graph of Thoughts (Yao et al., 2023; Besta et al., 2023) and ART (Paranjape et al., 2023) are listed in related work only.

CODE (snippets verbatim, location noted)
- p3 Fig 3d, generation, using a helper that has no definition:
  `num_fruits = 0` / `for object in objects:` / `object_is_fruit = is_fruit(object)` / `if object_is_fruit:` / `num_fruits += objects[object]` / `answer = num_fruits`
- Execution (p3 Fig 3e): after each line the trace prints `delta state: {object_is_fruit = True}`. The interpreter runs a line. If it raises an exception, the LM is shown the question, the prior lines and the state history, and produces the next state.
- p3 worked example: `answer = 0; answer += is_sarcastic('you don't say'); answer += 1;` -> Python sets {answer = 0}, the LMulator returns {answer = 1}, and Python finishes with {answer = 2}. The result is read from the variable `answer`.
- Few-shot coercion system message for chat models (A.4, p13): "Pretend you are a completion model that is prompted with three examples. You should follow the pattern of these examples strictly. At the end of your reply, you should always output an answer".
- Zero-shot CoC instruction (A.4): "write python code to help solve the problem, if it's helpful".
- No official code listing is given. The project page is https://chain-of-code.github.io/.

FIGURES
- Fig 1 (p1): a "countries visited" question over about 200 places. Direct answer and CoT give wrong answers, while CoC gives 52 (100%). The best one-glance explanation of CoC (needs `get_country` emulated by the LM, with `set()` and `len` run in Python).
- Fig 3 (p4): CoT vs PoT vs ScratchPad vs CoC generation and execution side by side, with the Python/LM split. This is the best figure for the note.
- Fig A2 (p17): "314 days after Valentine's Day", direct and CoT wrong (gpt-4, Oct 2023); CoC correct with `get_valentines_day_date` and `get_holiday` emulated. The authors note newer gpt-4 (Dec 2023) writes code and gets the same answer.
- Fig 4 (p6), Fig 5, 6 (p7), Fig 7 (p8): task-type, ablation, per-task and scaling plots. The values are only in the Table A1 text.
- Fig A1 (p16): the BBH worked traces, including Hyperbaton, Logical Deduction and Disambiguation QA.

PROBLEMS: No embedded instructions found. Extraction was clean except for spacing breaks and ligature loss ("T able", "W ei"), which do not affect numbers. Table 1 and Table 2 deltas are printed beside the number in the text. Plot values for Figs 2 and 4-7 are not extractable, so I did not report them. Table A3 columns are only partly labelled in the extraction (the header order is garbled). I mapped the labels from the caption: Direct, CoT, CoC (Python), CoC (LM) for each chat model. The gpt-4 "CoC (Python)=82" mapping is therefore from header order, not row labels. Check against the PDF if you cite it. The venue is confirmed from the page-1 footnote (ICML 2024, PMLR 235).
